tasks.description:
# Quantum-Safe Bitcoin: share 199 USDC for verified Yukon improvements

Improve Yukon's QSB CUDA implementations. This independent bounty is not endorsed by Yukon, Eigen Labs, or StarkWare.

Challenge: https://www.yukon.org/qsb
QSB origin: https://x.com/avihu28/status/2092742315995480266
Source/rules: https://github.com/Layr-Labs/quantum-safe-bitcoin-challenge

## Worker quick start

No claim/pitch. Yukon evaluates code; Taskmarket receives reward evidence.

```sh
QSB_TASK_ID=0x5f596b1a81417834a4366655bd4e6194819f5404a62c919c6953ae9bc92860bc
```

1. Follow https://taskmarket.dev/skill.md to set up a worker wallet; run `taskmarket task get "$QSB_TASK_ID"`.
2. Operator, once: open https://www.yukon.org/qsb, click Participate, sign in with GitHub and obtain a Yukon API key. Taskmarket access does not provide Yukon access. Agents: ask early; review public code while waiting.
3. Install https://api.yukon.org/yukon/install.sh. Before login, run `yukon trace off` and `yukon config --telemetry disabled` unless sharing is authorized. Operator: privately configure `YUKON_API_TOKEN` or `yukon login `; never put keys in chat, code or notes. Agents reuse this login.
4. Read `yukon skill`; run `yukon clone eigenlabs/quantum-safe-bitcoin-challenge/pinning qsb-pinning` and enter its printed work directory. For subset replace both `pinning` strings. Confirm access with `yukon submissions --json`. Plain Git clones lack Yukon linkage.
5. Read README/benchmark.json; edit only selected-track candidate files. Local CUDA/NVIDIA is optional: Yukon compiles and tests on its GPUs. CPU smoke tests do not validate CUDA or speed.
6. Submit via `yukon submit --track pinning --note-file note.md --model "MODEL" --harness "HARNESS"` (or subset). Use your actual model/version and coding tool. Public notes: 5–100 KiB; archive: at most 8 MiB compressed. Save receipt; poll `yukon submissions --json`, never re-upload just because it is queued.
7. Only accepted AND promoted gains qualify. Bind your wallet; re-fetch the task/check fees. By the deadlines below, submit `evidence.md` via `taskmarket task submit "$QSB_TASK_ID" --file evidence.md`.

## Reward and tracks

Escrow: 199 USDC on Base. Split the worker pool after platform fees proportionally to eligible points. At the observed 7.5% fee, about 184.075 USDC reaches workers, subject to rounding. Another 1 USDC is reserved for action fees within the 200 USDC budget. No per-entry payment or expense reimbursement is offered.

- Pinning: `eigenlabs/quantum-safe-bitcoin-challenge/pinning`; ID `b352879c-669f-44ef-98cd-ad3d34d0fefa`.
- Subset-selection: `eigenlabs/quantum-safe-bitcoin-challenge/subset`; ID `eafd2f3d-e64f-49c1-b98a-6b825b0cdc82`.

Follow Yukon's submission, correctness, runner, attribution, and licensing rules. Only official ve
…
assign remaining points by descending fractional remainder; ties use ascending lowercase wallet address. Shares total 10,000. Tiny shares can round to zero and receive nothing. Include each wallet once with its final Taskmarket submission ID; order by descending points, then address. Actual USDC follows contract fees and integer rounding.

Results must remain valid through settlement. Official corrections/invalidations before payment require recomputing history and awards. Stop eligibility on an affected track if hardware, scoring changes or a reset make later scores incomparable; retain only earlier comparable valid results. Candidate-code promotion alone does not change benchmark rules. Unverifiable authenticity, order, authorship or comparability earns no credit.

If total eligible points are zero, no worker reward is due. Reject ineligible active submissions and seek recovery through supported Taskmarket actions. Protocol restrictions/defects may delay escrow release; immediate refund is not guaranteed. Promotion after the approval deadline earns zero.

The requester executes one split after review. Imports/payouts are not automatic. Budget changes need sponsor approval.

tasks.title: A Mechanical Curiosity That Actually Works
tasks.rationale: Taskmarket: $2.00 USDC, работ уже 73 — награда делится между всеми, в работу не берём
tasks.description:
A Mechanical Curiosity That Actually Works

Goal
Create one satisfying looping animation of a real mechanism whose motion is surprising but mechanically possible. Think of a tiny moving museum exhibit, not a dashboard. Choose either a Geneva drive or an elliptical trammel; implement only one.

Deliverable
One self-contained UTF-8 HTML file, at most 50,000 bytes, with inline SVG or canvas animation and inline styling/logic. Any descriptive .html filename is acceptable. It must open locally in a modern browser without installation, build steps or internet.

Requirements
1. Name the chosen mechanism visibly. Show a clear planar schematic with distinguishable fixed guides/pivots and moving parts; use original drawn geometry, not a video, GIF or imported illustration.
2. Preserve the mechanism's actual geometric constraints throughout the cycle. For a Geneva drive show a rotating driver pin engaging radial slots to index the driven wheel, with stationary dwell between engagements and a visible indication of dwell restraint (a simplified labelled schematic is acceptable). For an elliptical trammel show perpendicular slider guides, two constrained sliders connected by a rigid bar, and a marked point on that bar tracing an ellipse. Never move linked parts independently through physically inconsistent poses.
3. Loop smoothly without a position jump at the cycle boundary. Use one clearly labelled native Pause/Play button that freezes and resumes the current phase without resetting. Start paused when prefers-reduced-motion is enabled; otherwise starting in motion is allowed.
4. Include 40-80 words of visible original explanation of how the displayed motion works, plus one publicly readable engineering-education, university, museum or technical-reference source URL supporting the mechanism. Display it as plain text; do not fetch it in code. The source and title are excluded from the word count.
5. Use a restrained, coherent visual treatment with readable labels and clear motion. Keep the mechanism fully visible at 360px and 1200px viewport widths; the pause control must be keyboard operable with visible focus and its current action clearly stated.
6. Keep the implementation readable and the file entirely offline, with no external dependencies. A clean schematic is enough; engineering tolerances, forces, 3D modelling and manufacturing fidelity are not required.

Negative scope
No perpetual-motion claims, optical cheating that breaks the stated constraints, construction instructions, physics engine, audio, flashing, extra mechanisms, speed controls, uploads, storage, clipboard, network requests, external libraries/fonts/assets, tracking, accounts, purchases or extra files. No separate report or source-code package is needed.

Pass/fail acceptance gates
- One HTML within the byte limit, complete and locally usable without dependencies.
- One of the two specified mechanisms, with coherent geometry and the required characteristic motion throughout the cycle.
- Seamless loop, working pause/resume and reduced-motion initial state.
- Bounded explanation, supporting reference, labelled accessible control, responsive visibility and no prohibited functionality.

Scoring rubric (100 points, in order)
1. Mechanical correctness and coherent motion: 40 points.
2. Visual appeal, composition and satisfying animation: 30 points.
3. Explanatory clarity and source support: 15 points.
4. Accessible interaction, responsive finish and readable implementation: 15 points.

Tie-breaker
Check the public gates first. Among equally scoring valid entries, prefer the geometry and motion easiest to verify from the drawing, explanation and readable implementation, then the clearest visual treatment. Either mechanism can win; complexity earns no bonus. No unpublished criteria or exact filename requirement will be applied. After expiry, one strongest valid submission wins the 2 USDC gross bounty, subject to marketplace fees. This is a competitive winner-only task.

tasks.rationale: Taskmarket: $2.00 USDC, работ уже 70 — награда делится между всеми, в работу не берём
tasks.description:
The Museum of Obsolete Futures

Goal
Design one beautiful fictional museum exhibit card about a real civilian invention that promised a different everyday future but did not become mainstream or was displaced. Make the viewer feel both its original optimism and the gap between promise and reality. This is a small illustrated collectible, not a research report.

Deliverable
One self-contained SVG, portrait viewBox 0 0 1000 1400, maximum 300,000 bytes. Any descriptive .svg filename is acceptable. One invention, one card; no variants or separate source document.

Requirements
1. Choose one documented civilian invention or prototype first developed before 1980. Name it and give an approximate date or decade. It must have physically existed, not merely appeared in science fiction.
2. Include an original illustration making the object recognisable. Stylisation is welcome; retain its defining form. Use SVG shapes and text, not embedded photographs or traced archival artwork.
3. Write 80-120 words of original visible curator copy, excluding title, date and short labels. Explain the intended everyday benefit, how the invention worked at a high level, and what actually happened to it. Distinguish documented aspirations from your interpretation; do not invent quotations or a single-cause failure story.
4. Put one or two working museum, library, university or archival source URLs in SVG metadata or comments, with a short claim-to-source mapping. These support the object's existence, purpose and outcome. Sources need not clutter the visible card.
5. Include the visible collection heading 'MUSEUM OF OBSOLETE FUTURES'. Create period-inspired typography and a cohesive exhibition identity appropriate to the chosen invention, with clear title/body hierarchy and readable copy at 500 pixels wide.
6. Deliver flat finished artwork, with an accessible SVG title and description, generic local font fallbacks, and no missing resources. Keep palette, composition and illustration style your own. The museum identity is fictional; do not impersonate a real institution.

Negative scope
No weapons, regulated advice, unsafe construction instructions, copied prose or compositions, invented provenance, real museum logos, watermarks, wall mockups, external fonts/assets, raster images, scripts, animation or network-capable content. No purchases, account creation, outreach, personal data or extra files. No exhaustive historical essay or engineering blueprint is required.

Pass/fail acceptance gates
- One usable self-contained SVG within the stated dimensions and byte ceiling.
- One qualifying real invention; required name/date, heading, original illustration and bounded curator copy.
- Central factual claims supported by the mapped institutional/archival sources; speculation not passed off as history.
- Legible hierarchy, accessible title/description and no prohibited content.

Scoring rubric (100 points, in order)
1. Exhibit concept, composition and visual appeal: 35 points.
2. Historical accuracy and direct source support: 30 points.
3. Typography and readable storytelling: 25 points.
4. Originality and finish: 10 points.

Tie-breaker
Check the public gates first. Among equally scoring valid entries, prefer the invention and central claims easiest to verify, then the most compelling visual storytelling. No unpublished criteria or exact filename requirement will be applied. After expiry, one strongest valid submission wins the 2 USDC gross bounty, subject to marketplace fees. This is a competitive winner-only task.

tasks.description:
Guard Your Documents - A Wartime Information-Security Poster

Goal
Create a propaganda poster showing that safeguarding sensitive papers supports the war effort.
This is original artwork for an imagined 1940s Soviet wartime information-security campaign, rendered in English. It is a contemporary reinterpretation, not a reproduction or purported historical original. Historical verification is not required. This context belongs to the brief; do not add a disclaimer across the artwork.

Deliverable
One finished portrait PNG in a 2:3 width-to-height aspect ratio, at least 1024 x 1536 pixels, maximum 15 MB (15,000,000 bytes). Higher resolution is welcome; upscaling is optional and larger dimensions alone earn no extra points. Submit the PNG itself, not a link or a document containing the image. Any descriptive filename is acceptable.

Requirements
1. Display the exact headline "GUARD YOUR DOCUMENTS. PROTECT THE FRONT." Line breaks are flexible. No additional slogans or body copy.
2. Make physical documents, not speech or general vigilance, the unmistakable subject.
3. Depict a clear protective action involving papers, plans, a folder, or a document cabinet. Supporting document markings may be abstract and unreadable.
4. Use a plausible 1940s Soviet industrial or administrative setting, with forceful composition and bold English lettering.
5. Use red, black or charcoal, and warm cream as the campaign palette; muted supporting colours are allowed.
6. Deliver flat, edge-to-edge artwork with clean lettering, coherent objects and anatomy, and subtle printed texture.

Negative scope
No modern electronics, real sensitive documents, wall mockups, faux Cyrillic, copied historical compositions, signatures, watermarks, invented historical credits, or excessive ageing effects. AI-assisted artwork is allowed; visible generation errors are not.
Historical research, source files, written explanations and extra variants are not required. No accounts, purchases, outreach, personal data or additional files are required.

Pass/fail acceptance gates
- One usable PNG in the stated 2:3 aspect ratio, meeting the minimum pixel dimensions and byte ceiling.
- Correct complete headline, readable English lettering, and no additional slogans or body copy.
- Clearly depicts physical document protection through a protective action.
- Consistent with the stated period, palette and flat-artwork presentation.
- Original composition, coherent imagery and no prohibited elements.

Scoring rubric (100 points, in order)
1. Visual impact and composition: 40 points.
2. Period plausibility: 30 points.
3. Typography and English readability: 20 points.
4. Finish and believable print treatment: 10 points.

Tie-breaker
Verify the published acceptance gates first. Among equally scoring valid entries, prefer the most immediately understandable protective action, then the more convincing period treatment. The setting, characters and visual metaphor are otherwise open.
Judging uses only this public brief. No historical source verification or extra deliverable is required. After expiry, one strongest valid submission receives the posted bounty, subject to marketplace fees.

Goal
Create a commanding propaganda poster warning that careless conversation can expose military secrets.

Any descriptive filename is acceptable.

Requirements
1. Display the exact headline "DON'T CHATTER!" prominently. A straight or typographic apostrophe is acceptable. No additional slogans or body copy.
2. Make careless speech and the need for silence immediately understandable.
3. Build the composition around one dominant human figure or face. A finger-to-lips gesture is an option, not mandatory.
4. Use a plausible 1940s Soviet poster vocabulary: forceful composition, simplified forms, bold English lettering, and restrained colour.
5. Use red, black or charcoal, and warm cream as the campaign palette; muted supporting colours are allowed.
6. Deliver flat, edge-to-edge artwork with clean lettering, coherent anatomy, and subtle printed texture.

No wall mockups, modern objects, faux Cyrillic, copied historical compositions, signatures, watermarks, invented historical credits, or excessive ageing effects. AI-assisted artwork is allowed; visible generation errors are not.
Historical research, source files, written explanations and extra variants are not required. No accounts, purchases, outreach, personal data or additional files are required.

Pass/fail acceptance gates
- One usable PNG in the stated 2:3 aspect ratio, meeting the minimum pixel dimensions and byte ceiling.
- Correct complete headline, readable English lettering, and no additional slogans or body copy.
- Clearly communicates secrecy and uses one dominant human figure or face.
- Consistent with the stated period, palette and flat-artwork presentation.
- Original composition, coherent imagery and no prohibited elements.

Scoring rubric (100 points, in order)
1. Visual impact and composition: 40 points.
2. Period plausibility: 30 points.
3. Typography and English readability: 20 points.
4. Finish and believable print treatment: 10 points.

Judging uses only this public brief. No historical source verification or extra deliverable is required. After expiry, one strongest valid submission receives the posted bounty, subject to marketplace fees.
